videos.script:
Lesson 9's client was twelve lines. It sends a query and reads the answer, and it forgets everything the moment it has. That is fine for one screen and one change.

{{cache}} A GraphQL client remembers. Apollo Client keeps every object it has seen in a cache, one entry per course and one per session, keyed by type and id. Ask again and it answers from memory. Change session six, and every query that showed session six sees the change.

{{node}} You will watch that happen from the terminal first, five steps against the lesson's server, printing what the cache holds after each.

{{planner}} Then the planner moves to Apollo. The screen subscribes to the cache, so it redraws whenever the cache changes. And when the server refuses a change, the client takes the screen back, on its own.

{{cost}} None of this is free. You will measure what Apollo adds to the build, and keep it out of the static one entirely.

{{relay}} And Relay, Meta's client, which asks more of the schema and the build in return for a stricter rule: each component declares exactly the data it reads.
